prompt:
Our biomedical AI assistant has been conducting research conversations with scientists over the past two weeks, and all those sessions have been saved as plain text transcripts in the `conversations/` folder of our project workspace at `/workspace`. The problem is that our assistant has no memory between sessions — every time it starts, it has no idea what was previously discussed about compounds, researchers, or experimental results.

We need you to set up a persistent memory system so that:
1. The workspace is properly initialized for long-term memory tracking.
2. All three conversation transcripts are processed to extract named entities (compounds, researchers, findings) into a queryable knowledge structure.
3. Events are scored for novelty/importance and any conflicting information across transcripts is reconciled.
4. A session-startup context file called `RECALL-CONTEXT.md` is generated in the workspace root, ready to be injected at the beginning of each new assistant session.

The goal is that when the assistant starts its next session, it can immediately recall that Veratromine inhibits KX-7 at multiple measured IC50 values, that Synaptinol failed hepatotoxicity screening, that Neuroflux has an unexpected serotonin receptor binding, and who the key researchers involved are. Everything should work fully offline with no external API calls.
